newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian, Trinidad businesmen agree to promote trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian, Trinidad businesmen agree to promote trade.

text.p: Businessmen from India and Trinadad and Tobago signed an agreement on Tuesday to promote trade and investment between the two countries.
The Federation of Indian Export Organisations (FIEO) and the Trinidad and Tobago Chamber of Industry and Commerce signed a memorandum of understanding in the Indian capital.
"The parties shall take the opportunities available to them to promote trade and investment between India and Trinadad and Tobago mutually," the agreement said.
Businessmen said vast opportunities existed for Indian firms to set up joint ventures in Trinidad and Tobago and create a base for trade with Latin American countries.

"The Indian enterpreneurs can establish joint ventures with the local firms in the country and use it as a base for trading with the South American markets," FIEO director general R.K. Dhawan told a meeting of the two trade groups.

Last week, visiting Trinidad and Tobago Prime Minister Basdeo Panday, in India on a two-week official visit, said his country was a good platform for Indian businessmen to launch into South American markets.
India's trade with Latin America rose 160 percent to 31.4 billion in 1995/96 (April-March) from 12.0 billion rupees in 1990/91, industry officials said.

"They (Trinidad and Tobago businessmen) will be looking at general imports and exports, pharmaceuticals including medical and hospital supplies, textiles and garments," Michael Arneaud, president of the Trinidad and Tobago Chamber of Commerce and Industry, said.

India's exports to Trinidad and Tobago in April-September 1996 were valued at $2.78 million against $1.52 million in the same period in 1995. Imports from Trinidad and Tobago grew to $1.32 million during April-September 1996 from some $10,000 in the same period in 1995.
Indian exports to Trinidad and Tobago consist mainly of engineering goods, textiles, chemical products, rubber and plastic products, gems and jewellery and sports goods.
India mainly imports non-ferrous metals, wood and wood products from Trinidad and Tobago.
Businessmen from Trinidad and Tobago said they are promoting investment in areas such as food processing, aquaculture, computer and software, hotel and tourism.
Arneaud said Trinidad and Tobago's exports to India lagged well behind the Caribbean island's imports from India.
"As a result, we feel there is enormous scope for growth and development in exports to India," he said.
Arneaud said Trinidad and Tobago actively supported the the formation of the Free Trade Area of the Americas (FTAA), expected to come into operation by 2005.
"FTAA will create the largest free trade area in the world stretching from Canada in the north to Tierra del Fuego in the south with a market of more than 450 million people," Arneaud said.
